Pawan Upadhyay And Another vs State Of U.P. on 22 March,
2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Court No. - 88
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 9912 of 2023
Applicant :- Pawan Upadhyay And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ravindra Prakash Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicants is taken on record.

Heard Sri Ravindra Prakash Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicants and Dr. S.B. Maurya,
learned AGA-I for the State-respondent.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicants on bail in Case Crime No. 102 of 2022, under Sections 406, 420, 323, 384, 506 IPC, Police Station- Dubauliya, District- Basti,
during pendency of the trial in the court below.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicants have been falsely implicated in the present matter by the informant and actually applicants were the victim and informant received Rs.
3 lacs from him and others under the false promise to provide job to them in FCI in the year 2013 but neither applicants could get the job nor the money of the applicants were returned and thereafter under the pressure of the applicants in the year 2019 informant prepared a notary affidavit and he admitted that he received total Rs. 3 lacs from the applicants and others and out of 3 lacs he returned only Rs. 25,000 and he assured that he will return rest of the amount but in spite of Pawan Upadhyay And Another vs State Of U.P. on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8683668/
1 that he failed to return the rest of the amount.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submitted that on 2.3.2022 informant moved an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
against applicants and others with the allegation that in the year 2019 he never gave any notary affidavit and entire notary affidavit is totally false and baseless.
He further submitted that as informant duped the applicants and therefore, with only intention to save his skin, informant falsely implicated the applicants in the present matter.
Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that with regard to payment of Rs. 3 lacs a dispute is pending between the applicants and informant.
I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

From the perusal of the record it appears that FIR of the present case was lodged on the basis of application moved by the informant under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and during the pendency of application moved under Section 156(3) FIR was lodged by one of the co-accused against the informant and as per the allegation made by him informant duped him, applicants and others and he received Rs. 3 lacs from them and under the false promise to provide job to them in FCI and therefore, it appears that some dispute with regard to payment of Rs. 3 lacs is pending between applicant and informant and form the perusal of allegation made against the applicants in the present case it appears that on the basis of vague and general allegation they have been made accused in the present matter, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case in my view applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicants- Pawan Upadhyay and Ankit Shukla be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicants shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicants.
